results.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks | TechCrunch
results.content:
With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.

The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says. [...] Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.

Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow.

As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines. [...] The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time.

When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says.

Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile.

The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet.

results.title: Anthropic targets workplace collaboration with Claude Meetings – Computerworld
results.content:
One of the new tools announced Tuesday is Claude Meetings. This lets users add Claude to video meetings, where it takes notes, answers questions in the call’s chat interface, retrieves information from connected apps, and creates project plans and timelines. After a call, notes and action items are available in claude.ai, the browser-based version of Claude. Claude Meetings is reportedly accessible only in Google Meet currently; Anthropic hasn’t responded to a request for further details

The launch of Claude Meetings highlights the “continued value of leveraging context within meetings to improve workflows,” said Irwin Lazar, principal analyst at Metrigy. [...] Claude Meetings has similar functionality to existing meeting assistants, such as Copilot in Microsoft Teams, Zoom My Notes, and Webex’s meeting agent, he said, and also competes with standalone meeting assistants, such as Otter and Granola.

“As Claude increasingly becomes the place where people are doing their work, it makes sense for Claude to have direct access to meeting notes without requiring cut/paste, or MCP access, which vendors like Zoom now charge for,” said Lazar. [...] news analysis

# Introducing Claude Meetings

Add Claude to your video call and get the work started while you talk

 CategoryProduct updates
 ProductClaude Cowork
 DateNovember 12, 2026
 Reading time5 min
 Share

Claude can now join your video calls as a visible participant, following the conversation and starting on work during the meeting. Claude Meetings is now in beta.

Your team can ask Claude questions during the meeting, out loud or in chat. By default, Claude answers in writing, and it can use your connected tools with your permission.

Claude also works with you live to build docs, whiteboards (opens in new tab), or other artifacts, while teammates on the invite refine them. Claude writes the notes and action items, so no one on the call has to. [...] Claude Meetings is starting to roll out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Support for other video conferencing platforms is coming soon.

## What it looks like

Say your team is planning a customer event, and Claude is on the call. You say, “Claude, start a doc for this plan.” Claude writes up what the team has said so far, and teammates on the invite can edit the plan while you keep talking.

When you start discussing the budget, someone asks Claude what last year’s event cost. Claude asks for their approval to look it up, posts it in the meeting chat, and compares it to the current plan. When you start discussing timelines, someone asks Claude to put it on a whiteboard, and the team works on the schedule alongside the doc. [...] Before the meeting ends, someone asks Claude to share a recap with the team. After the call, any notes, action items, plan, and whiteboard are on the meeting’s page in claude.ai (opens in new tab).

Later, you can go back to meetings you were part of and ask Claude about them, or add Claude to the next one from your calendar in claude.ai.

We’re working with partners like Gong, Attention, Granola, Fireflies.ai, and Otter so you’ll soon be able to send a meeting’s transcript to the tools your team already uses.

results.title: How to Generate Municipal Meeting Minutes with Claude | ClerkMinutes
results.content:
#### Step 1: Pick the right Claude model

Just like ChatGPT, the free version of Claude limits message count, file uploads and model power. For minutes, especially long ones, you’ll want the paid plan so you can access Sonnet or Opus without hitting limits. That’s $20 per month.

We recommend Claude Sonnet 5 for the vast majority of meeting minutes. It's fast, accurate, affordable, and handles 1M token context windows. Claude Opus 4.8 is the right choice for the most complex multi-hour meetings where you need maximum reasoning depth.

#### Step 2: Paste your agenda before anything else

Claude needs to understand the structure of the meeting before it reads the discussion. Otherwise, it will try to infer agenda items based on topic similarities, which can cause blending. [...] Here’s what makes Claude different from other AI tools.

1. Claude can handle very long meetings without losing the thread.

The newest models, Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Opus 4.8, can read extremely long transcripts in one go. They support context windows of up to 1 million tokens, which is just a technical way of saying, "You can upload a massive transcript and Claude won't forget what happened earlier in the meeting."

This makes a big difference for clerks dealing with:

 Four-hour council meetings
 Complex planning discussions
 Public comment marathons
 Budget hearings with multiple speakers

Claude is simply harder to overwhelm. [...] Built for municipal compliance  
- Claude (Sonnet 5): No  
- ClerkMinutes: Yes

Now that you’ve seen both workflows side by side, the pattern becomes pretty clear. Claude is powerful, but it still behaves like an all-in-one tool. It can summarize, rewrite, reorganize, and help you think through meetings quickly, but only after you feed it everything in the right order, give it the right instructions, and double-check the output carefully.

ClerkMinutes, on the other hand, is built for the exact work clerks do every day. It already understands agendas, motions, seconds, amendments, votes, and municipal formatting. That’s why the workflow is shorter and the review process is more predictable.
